text:
Alex: Heads up — I'm prototyping a lenient fallback for fncall schema rejects. Instead of returning a hard 400, route to a permissive model variant that tries to coerce/repair the output and then emit a sanitized tool invocation. Thoughts?

Maria: Billing and UX concerns. If we do extra execution behind the scenes, do we charge the customer twice? they'll notice spikes.

Samir: Implementation note: our pipeline currently bills on the final outbound token usage. Routing an extra permissive run will add compute + tokens. We can either: 1) bill both attempts, 2) bill only the final, or 3) bill final + a small surcharge metric. Need product input.

Olivia: Telemetry needs to capture the decision tree. Proposal: emit metadata for every validation event: `validation.reason`, `validation.score`, `validation.mode` (strict|lenient), `fallback.variant`, `trace_id`, and `sampled_original_payload` (sampled at route-level). Full payloads should be sampled (PII concerns).

Alex: Example of the kind of validator error triggering this: ```ValidationError: missing required field 'items[0].price' at /body/items/0/price``` In many cases the permissive pass can infer price from `line_total` or fall back to `estimate_price()` and succeed.

Maria: Console UX request: add a "Structured output issues" card on the route dashboard that shows recent rejects, grouped by reason, with a small sandbox pane where SRE/product can click "re-run permissive" on a sampled example. Also show delta in cost pre/post fallback.

Samir: Big question: do we change the HTTP contract? Right now a schema reject => 400. If we return a repaired invocation (202 or 200) some clients will treat it as success even though we changed the tool args. Suggest making it opt-in at route level: `allow_partial_fncall: true|false`. Default false.

Olivia: For billing transparency, add a separate meter `fncall.fallback_exec` that increments when permissive fallback runs. Expose it in the console and in usage exports. That avoids confusing token attribution in the main meter.

deploy-bot: [staging] flag `fncall-fallback-permissive` queued for deploy to staging cluster.

qa-bot: QA plan: add unit tests for validator + permissive-shim, integration tests for headers and billing meter propagation, and an e2e that verifies trace_id links original->fallback->final.

Alex: Edge case: if the permissive variant ends up invoking a different tool (e.g., `refund_estimator` -> `manual_review`), we must retain an audit trail showing original requested tool and final invoked tool. telemetry.trace_id must be in every related event.

Maria: Quota semantics: do we decrement user quota on the original attempt or on final executed tool? My vote: decrement on final invocation to avoid double charging, but we need to show estimated cost upfront.

Samir: Counterpoint: if permissive fallback is expensive and we only decrement final, customers may accidentally skirt quota by forcing permissive fallbacks. We should add an upfront header `X-Estimated-Exec-Cost` with the expected range and a flag `X-Fallback-Applied` in the response when fallback was used.

Olivia: Rollout plan suggestion: behind flag per-route -> 24h canary on internal accounts -> 10% account cohort -> evaluate metrics: validation.rate, fallback.rate, cost.delta, and support.tickets mentioning unexpected charges.

Alex: Can someone sketch the minimal telemetry object we can ship behind the flag (100% metadata, 0.1% full payload sampling)? A small example would help the console team.

Olivia: Sample telemetry keys (to send as event):
```
{
  "trace_id": "uuid",
  "route": "orders.create",
  "validation.reason": "missing_field_items_0_price",
  "validation.score": "0.0",
  "validation.mode": "lenient",
  "fallback.variant": "inference-coerce-v1",
  "fallback_cost_estimate": "0.003-0.007",
  "final_tool": "price_updater",
  "sampled_original_payload_present": "true|false"
}
```
(we'll stringify and flatten keys in the event payload)

Maria: Alerts: spike in `validation.rate` > 0.5% on a route for 30m -> page on-call. Also create a low-severity alert for `fallback_rate` > 2% for 1h to catch regressions.

Samir: I'll take ownership of console meter integration and the `X-Estimated-Exec-Cost` header. I'll prototype the header format: `X-Estimated-Exec-Cost: tokens=50-120;usd=0.002-0.006;note=fallback_possible`

Alex: One more UX ask: surface whether the fallback changed the tool arguments in the response metadata (e.g., `x-fallback-changed-args: true`) so SDKs can surface a warning. We should also add an opt-out header customers can set: `Prefer: strict-fncall` to force 400.

Olivia: I'll draft the rollout doc and console card mockups. QA — please include a support playbook on how to interpret telemetry samples before we flip default.

Samir: PR coming for the meter and header changes, cc @Maria for billing language.

Alex: Thanks all. Can someone open the tracking ticket in the eng-platform board and link the staging flag? Assign @Samir to console pieces and @Maria to billing alerts.

Maria: On it — creating ticket now and adding the alert rules as a follow-up.

Samir: Got it. Will ping once header prototype is live in staging.

Olivia: Thanks — tagging product for decision on default (probably opt-in for now).

Alex: Great. Closing for now.
